ready-file.name: The Ready File
ready-file.tagline: The paperwork, finished and in your hands, in 48 hours.
ready-file.bestFor: You can run your own appointments — you just need the file to be right.
features: Your route confirmed against your own authorisation and entry stamp
Your EX-17 or EX-18, pre-filled, flattened and print-ready
Modelo 790 Código 012 set for cash, with a named branch and its counter hours
Your Padrón file, prepared for the council you actually live in
If the flat isn’t in your name, the authorisation form for the owner to sign
Padrón and TIE/CUE appointments searched and booked in your own name
Every copy made, collated in counter order, and audited line by line

soft-landing.name: The Soft Landing
soft-landing.tagline: The paperwork, plus the cards you should already be holding.
soft-landing.bestFor: Most students who landed in the last few weeks and are still buying single tickets.
features: A T-mobilitat card in your name with 90 days loaded — T-jove if you’re under 30
Your Carnet Jove, applied for, paid, and chased through the activation wait
Your ISIC card, bought and issued against your enrolment evidence
A bank account that actually receives money from home — or why you need none
SIM or eSIM matched to your real usage, with the 28-day renewal trap explained
A WhatsApp line for 30 days, in English, through the window questions come up
A live line during your appointment: call us from the counter

fixer.name: The Fixer
fixer.tagline: Everything above, plus we turn up.
fixer.bestFor: You’re stuck on the padrón, or still signing for a flat and want it read first.
features: We come to the town hall with you, and translate
The padrón unlock: hostels, sublets, a refusing landlord, the wrong municipality
Your health card and a local GP who speaks English, once the padrón is through
Same-day contract review before you sign, checked against the statutory deposit cap
Ownership verified at the registry — holding keys is not proof of ownership
Move-in condition report: every defect photographed, signed, sent the same day
90-day tracking through to collection, and a completion report for whoever’s paying

page.metaDescription: Three fixed-fee packages for international students already in Barcelona: The Ready File, The Soft Landing, and The Fixer. Two prices per package — one for the EU route, one for the non-EU route.
page.title: Fixed fees for a process with no fixed timeline.
page.intro: Every package is quoted exclusive of IVA and shown with its total including {rate}% IVA before you pay. Nothing is billed hourly, and no package includes government fees.
page.routesTitle: The EU route is less work, so we charge less for it.
page.routesBody: No fingerprints, no €16.08 tasa, and where the requirements are met the certificate is normally issued at the appointment itself. Non-EU students need the EX-17, the biometric appointment, and at some offices a separate collection trip. We confirm which route applies to you at triage, before you pay anything.
page.govTitle: The one payment we cannot make for you.
page.honestTitle: The things that cause complaints, said up front.

honest.item: The 790 arrives unpaid, and it has to
honest.note: It’s a barcoded form that must be carried to a bank counter or scanner, paid, and stamped. Online settlement needs a Spanish digital certificate you don’t have yet. We configure it, print it and tell you exactly where to take it — the trip is yours. An unstamped form ends the appointment.

honest.item: Our copies are printed copies, not certified ones
honest.note: We print from the scans you upload. We have never seen your original passport and cannot certify anything. You carry the originals; the folder carries what accompanies them.

honest.item: We cannot make an appointment exist
honest.note: We search the official portal for up to six weeks from your submission. September and October are the worst of it — the government systems saturate and slots are gone in minutes. If none opens in that window you get 50% back and keep the entire Ready File — forms, copies, 790, audit — so you’re ready the day one does. If a deadline of yours passes first, we give you a dated certificate of every attempt we made; Spanish offices commonly accept that as justification for registering late, though no official is obliged to. Nobody can shortcut this step legally, and any service that tells you otherwise is selling you something it doesn’t have.

honest.item: We don’t attend the biometric appointment for you
honest.note: It requires you, in person, with originals. We prepare, book, brief, and stay reachable on the phone. The appearance is yours, in your own name.

honest.item: Your 90 days start when you tap
honest.note: The T-jove window runs from first validation, not from purchase. But it’s 90 consecutive days once it starts, not 90 days of use.

honest.item: T-jove is an age rule, not a student rule
honest.note: Under 30 only. No university card or Carnet Jove needed to qualify. If you’re thirty or over we load T-usual for the zones your commute actually needs, and the difference comes back to you.

page.exclusionsTitle: What our fee does not cover.

exclusions.note: Paid by you, directly, at a bank. The amount is set by the government and varies by card type.
We never handle funds for third parties. Everything goes directly from you to the landlord or the institution.
Outside our scope. If your case needs it, we will say so and point you to a colegiado abogado.
We identify what needs it and refer you to a traductor jurado; their fee is separate.
